Look, I know I'll be attacked over this point, but having a reserve bank is a good thing that is absolutely required by a modern economy.

Why?

Imagine two nations go to war. X nation uses gold backed currency while Y nation uses a reserve bank. X nation only has the money it has to pay for the war effort, any other money it needs, it must seek externally. Y nation can borrow from itself, without needing to seek external lenders.

How does a reserve bank do this? Rather than basing the currency on shares of a tangible asset, like gold, the currency is reflective of a share of the overall economy. Too much debt and you end up with strong deflationary pressure which slows economic growth. Too little debt and you tend to have inflationary problems.

What is this debt? How can you have debt for money created out of thin air? Well, it's not actually created out of thin air. The fed auctions off bonds. These bonds pay different interest rates, the more reliable your credit, the lower the rates tend to be.

Grossly simplified example... Fed has great credit and issues a $100 bond at 1% interest, which means they can now create $100 new dollars, with $99 dollars entering the economy. If the fed has poor credit and interest rates rise (so from a failure to raise the debt ceiling) to 10%, that same $100 bond now only creates $90 new dollars.

The fed debt isn't that important, as long as it can keep paying for its issues, which it can do so long as the overall economy is in reasonable health.
